the muon multiplicity in the energy range of 10 6 - 10 7 GeV is a sensitive probe to the primary mass composition.
the multi-muon data can be used to identify the average primary mass composition and that the multi-mue events are linked to high multiplicity fluctuations in high-energy collisions.

multi-muon event configurations are sensitive to primary mass composition, and the average properties and topology are useful for identifying average primary mass composition, which is a key to understanding the origin of the ultra-high-energy cosmic rays.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics.

the physics of ultra-high-energy collisions and the physics of deep underground multi-muon experiments, with the ultimate aim of identifying primary cosmic-ray mass composition in the energy range above 1016 GeV.
the study of the properties of ultra-high energy cosmic-ray showers in the atmosphere and the detection of the secondary particles deep underground.

multi-muon studies at the Gran Sasso Laboratory can provide a unique and complementary information on the mass composition of cosmic rays in the energy range from 106-107GeV.
the observed multi-muon event configurations are compatible with the hypothesis that the primary mass composition is dominated by protons and light nuclei.
multi-muon studies at deep underground laboratories are a powerful method to study ultra-high-energy collisions, and to determine the mass composition of cosmic rays.

a deep underground experiment is an ideal tool for the study of high-energy collisions.

the multi-muon event rate at the Gran Sasso underground laboratory (LNGS) is not sensitive to the mass composition, but it is sensitive to the energy spectrum.
